poems.title: Out of Life
poems.why: evening into night; the fire escape at dusk
poems.sound: Flickering 8mm reel showing a birthday, a goodbye, a silent stare.

scenes.name: The reading
scenes.what: POET reads the poem aloud to the EX; the TV shows the world's chaos.
scenes.camera: static wide of the bare room, POET in the foreground, window and EX's back deep in frame; insert on the TV
scenes.here: the Severn, a high bedroom; the Hive's needles fill the window

scenes.name: Haze at the window
scenes.what: EX vapes on the fire escape, back always turned; haze builds; POET moves toward the window but the EX gets further away.
scenes.camera: slow push toward the window that never closes the distance (dolly-zoom feel), haze softening focus
scenes.here: the window and the iron escape; the Orange Catwalk runs 30 m below

scenes.name: Off the fire escape
scenes.what: EX falls off the fire escape into darkness; POET falls behind into the clouds until it is black. Title card.
scenes.camera: over-the-railing high angle as the EX drops, then POV fall through cloud to black; hold black for title
scenes.here: the escape's top landing over the light well

scenes.name: The fall montage
scenes.what: POET falls behind EX through images of world chaos swapping with ways people escape: drugs, partying, TV, media, phones.
scenes.camera: top-down falling bodies with projected/composited imagery streaming past; EX always seen from behind
scenes.here: below the tower, into the black

scenes.name: Crashing the vintage party
scenes.what: POET crashes into an old-time party in romantic slow motion; he chases the EX through the crowd but the EX keeps vanishing.
scenes.camera: handheld through the crowd at overcranked speed, light leaks, EX glimpsed back-to-camera then gone
scenes.here: the vintage party met mid-fall

scenes.name: Hole in the floor
scenes.what: POET stumbles through a hole in the party floor and keeps falling into pure blackness.
scenes.camera: low floor-level angle on his feet catching the edge, then overhead as he drops away into black
scenes.here: the hole in the party floor

lines.text: What we've made we don't want, what we've sold to the world, to ourselves, doesn't exist.
I look for a way out through the hallways, within the drawers and fire escapes, trip
on my own words, falling out of life, and find where you go when you leave.
It was the maze constructed by a tainted love, a known yet unknown pit beneath the quicksands
of the make-believe haven, and hidden in the overnourished forest of escapism that calls
for you.
At this age, I'll follow, following the full distance between us almost having it all and
starting anew, to rediscover when love was real.
I failed at protecting you from your own vices, crashing the party of your evilest instincts
to find vibrations that echo in silence, love and hate languages that translate and slow
dripping blood salivating on imminent doubts, fully awakening to our darkest nights.
Pause for a second, a spectrum of fields will thread needles of garments made of sweet memories
and photographs, film and fiction that leave me empty.
With your back faced against me, you offer me a new pursuit of happiness as I stumble
on my own words, landing into the secret of where you go when you leave, and I fall
out of life.

poems.title: Flashing Lights
poems.sound: Sirens muffled behind glass turn to thin whispers.

scenes.name: Falling with headlights off
scenes.what: POET in black space, falling or floating, lights flashing; EX in distress floats nearby, unreachable.
scenes.camera: floating wide in a black stage, strobing practicals; EX kept back-to-camera at a fixed unreachable distance
scenes.here: the black below the floor

scenes.name: Eyes dilate
scenes.what: Everything still black; his eyes dilate trying to see, then the camera pushes into and through them into the flashback.
scenes.camera: extreme close-up on the POET's eye, pupil opening, macro push-through into the next scene
scenes.here: his eye

scenes.name: Car pulls up
scenes.what: Young POET at the living-room window watches a car pull up, its lights flashing through the room because of the angle and the bumps in the road.
scenes.camera: from behind the child at the window, headlight beams sweeping across walls and ceiling
scenes.here: the child's living-room window over the curb, the road winding down past the towers

scenes.name: The ghost child
scenes.what: A ghost kid appears and hugs Young POET, telling him his parents' marriage won't last, then disappears.
scenes.camera: soft two-shot at child height, ghost slightly diffused; frost breath on the windowpane insert
scenes.here: beside the window

scenes.name: Parents arguing in the car
scenes.what: Ghost gone, Young POET stays at the window watching his parents argue in the car, curtains pulled and blinds up, left home alone.
scenes.camera: over-the-shoulder through the glass to the lit car interior; reverse close-up on the child's face in headlight wash
scenes.here: the window looking down to the curb

scenes.name: Tambourine through the window
scenes.what: The ghost child hands Young POET a tambourine; he throws it through the window, shattering the glass.
scenes.camera: high-speed glass shatter from outside looking in, tambourine exiting toward camera
scenes.here: the window itself

lines.text: I heard a scream for help while falling with my headlights off.
It was a type of silent scream a trap lover makes to escape a pending marriage,
a concussion, a set of walls caving inward, seething and simmering,
and a solitude of crowds and smiles.
I received an emergency call while tossing and turning.
It was a type of silent call a man makes to the mirror after midnight.
To digest the truth, a windless insomnia and epiphany of a road winding down.
After a day of life dilated at the sun as long and as wise as possible, we won't make it.
I was six I recall when the ghost of a dead and loveless seven-year-old child appeared
and shared that my parents marriage wouldn't last.
It was a type of warm and heavy breeze in winter
where a child is left home alone.
With curtains pulled and blinds up as far and as wise as possible to see flashing lights
and the whispering screams of two souls on a road winding down.
And no tears and no fucks, no love to give, old to teach.

poems.title: How to Break off an Engagement
poems.audio: audio/03_How to Break off an Engagement_mixdown_RY_250626.mp3

scenes.name: Tambourine through the chapel window

scenes.name: The empty temple
scenes.what: Close-ups of an empty sanctuary in time-lapse decay: choir stands, kneelers, a dry baptism pool, pews veiled in cobwebs, ash drifting.
scenes.camera: locked-off time-lapse plates and macro close-ups on wood, stone and web
scenes.here: the nave, choir loft and baptistery as built

scenes.name: Gifts at the side doors
scenes.what: Opened gift boxes left outside the side doors; spirits leave; ivy creeps over the cracked threshold.
scenes.camera: low exterior angle on the threshold, time-lapse of boxes weathering
scenes.here: the side doors and stone threshold

scenes.name: The storm
scenes.what: Thunder; a heavy storm takes over and speeds the decay until nothing remains.
scenes.camera: wide exterior time-lapse of the chapel silhouette in lightning, pulling back as it is washed away
scenes.here: the flat, from the beach

scenes.name: Remnants on the shore
scenes.what: Storm ends; what is left of the chapel lies on the shore with soaked bread, soiled blankets and footprints in mud.
scenes.camera: still wides of wreckage at the tide line, inserts on bread, blanket and mud prints
scenes.here: the tide line where the chapel stood

scenes.name: Tambourine shatters
scenes.what: The tambourine finally lands on the ground of the chapel remnants and shatters.
scenes.camera: slow-motion ground-level impact, fragments scattering toward lens
scenes.here: the chapel's remnant floor

lines.text: Old to forever, a tambourine sounds off an empty temple, empty choir stands, empty prayer lines, and abandoned Baptist pools,
pews taken by cobwebs, and doused in disintegration.
Spirits have left salvations and opened gift boxes placed outside the side doors.
It thunders, then it rains until nothing remains.
Old to the storm ending, what was once love now goods,
broken and sealed apart by lightning,
daily breads soaked and delivered rotted by rain,
and blankets soiled by venomous puppeteers,
old to two sets of button-printed footsteps,
and a tambourine shattered into pieces.

poems.title: Nevermore
poems.why: twilight deepening to full dark; moonlight

scenes.name: Shore of broken pieces
scenes.what: POET stands on the shore at night, hands in pockets, no heart; walks looking at the decay and shattered pieces as ravens fly overhead.
scenes.camera: lateral tracking along the tide line, POET in silhouette, ravens crossing; hands never shown
scenes.here: the shore below the rail, where the chapel's pieces washed east

scenes.name: The silence
scenes.what: Waves calm, wind stops, trees go still: the setting holds its breath.
scenes.camera: locked-off wides of sea and tree line, minimal motion
scenes.here: the shore looking out, then back to the trees

scenes.name: The heart on the sand
scenes.what: POET finds his heart on the shore; without using his hands it floats and re-enters him.
scenes.camera: low angle from the sand up past the glowing heart to the POET's chest; it rises into frame and in
scenes.here: on the sand at the foot of the shore steps

scenes.name: Trail up the incline
scenes.what: POET sees a trail and follows it up from the shore to the field, ravens overhead.
scenes.camera: crane or drone rising with him up the dune path, sea dropping behind
scenes.here: the trail up the steps and the incline to the field

scenes.name: Night garden field
scenes.what: Walking through the moonlit field, hands still in pockets; golden plants turn toward him, weeds recoil into shadow.
scenes.camera: wide moonlit field with the POET small in rows; reverse on blooms turning toward lens
scenes.here: the Night Garden Field

scenes.name: Searching for hands
scenes.what: Clouds hide the stars; POET searches the bare ground in the shadows for his two hands, finds them and puts them back on.
scenes.camera: near-black low-key shots skimming bare soil; payoff close-up as the hands return (first time hands are seen)
scenes.here: a bare patch in the field

scenes.name: Standing in the field
scenes.what: POET stands in the field reflecting, heart and hands restored, then is told to go.
scenes.camera: static frontal medium-wide, still tree and field behind; slow push in
scenes.here: the centre of the field by the lone tree

lines.text: What if I follow this trail to where the broken pieces have washed ashore and the ashes of expired wildfires
cover sands and debris
lift it from the night seawater's floor.
The waves will calm to fold it whispers and the winds will mute the trees for the right level of silence
to find a throbbing heart left at the midlife corner returned toward the incline.
A familiar heart
which has shaken off every sad blue note life can perform
to overcome and spread inspiration
and it used to be mine. I'll lift it with care putting it back in place and tell myself
nevermore.
What if I follow this reclaimed heart to where the puzzle pieces of faith are handcrafted
scrambled and scattered as mustard seas into the vast moonlight night's field.
The plants in a golden hue bloom and face toward me in anticipation.
The weeds repel falling into the shadows where our memories hide and mean so little in moments of defeat
as I'm called forward.
The clouds meet the stars for the deepest level of darkness welcoming extra hard work
to search for the bare ground for two hands. Hands that once could tusk dusk after dusk
find and celebrate a new life and feel good
and they too used to be mine.
I put them back on with the care of my future at stake and say to myself
nevermore. I've wanted the world and lost my soul.
I want nothing more than to just be myself and nothing more
and be alright. I do believe I'll be alright.
This reclaimed and dust settled heart rediscovered but dusted hands remind me
but say to me in this still muted tree in night garden feels silence
nevermore.
Now go.

scenes.name: The field goes still
scenes.what: POET stands in the field with his newly restored hands; the parade's first figures appear on the path ahead (inferred blocking).
scenes.camera: wide static on the field at night, POET small at center, procession lights entering from the far edge
scenes.here: the field's edge where 04 ended

scenes.name: Naming stars
scenes.what: Ancestors meet and accept the POET and hand him stars, then whole galaxies, as small held lights.
scenes.camera: medium tracking alongside POET as he walks into the parade; inserts of hands passing points of light
scenes.here: the avenue through the field

scenes.name: Southern-pine basement (memory)
scenes.what: The past 'was waiting': a humid basement used as a shared bedroom, mattress pads under pine beams that did not comfort his spine. Staged as memory, not a separate place (inferred).
scenes.camera: low-angle insert up at exposed pine joists, shallow focus, then match-cut back to the night sky
scenes.here: memory: the Southern-pine basement

scenes.name: Universes and blessings
scenes.what: The ancestors give him a universe to invent and the right to grant blessings and miracles where the spoken word is needed.
scenes.camera: slow push-in on POET's face as galaxies are placed in his hands; crowd of ancestors soft behind
scenes.here: the heart of the parade

scenes.name: Blood through the hands
scenes.what: POET looks at the hands he just recovered in Nevermore; the ancestral blood and fingerprints now run through them. The parade's sound swells (inferred).
scenes.camera: extreme close-up of palms and fingerprints lit by star-glow, rack focus to the ancestors
scenes.here: the far end of the parade, facing the city

scenes.name: Baritone and warning
scenes.what: His voice deepens to a baritone of a million cries; on 'beware' he turns from the parade toward the horizon where the Atlantis entrance waits (inferred).
scenes.camera: low-angle hero medium, POET turning out of frame toward the gate light
scenes.here: the trailhead at the Perimeter

lines.text: They tell me to ask if I can inherit the earth,
to ask if I can name my own stars, even galaxies if I may.
The past too was waiting for me.
Coming of age in the shared rooms of human basements
as bedrooms, mattress pads where the wood beams
of southern pine could comfort my spine, it didn't.
To dream was to prevail.
They tell me to ask if I can invent a new universe,
to ask if God would let me, little old me,
award a blessing here or there.
Even grant miracles where the needs
of the spoken word exists.
In uncertain times, in forsaken times,
in tears that spoke in lieu of forbidden lines,
or a history too battered and bruised to travel.
To dream was to prevail.
Their blood flows through my hands.
Fingerprints that orchestra great powers,
they tell me, sun kissing my skin
and deepening my voice to a baritone of a million cries,
to an unanswered plight.
Beware of me.

poems.title: Resurrecting Atlantis
poems.sound: Streaks of light traversing the night sky.

scenes.name: The Light Gates open
scenes.what: Marble gates with wings swing open to an ancestral orchestra; a line of figures, the POET among them, walks through into the radiant city.
scenes.camera: low wide on the gates opening, POET entering frame from behind camera; reverse to the city glowing through
scenes.here: the Light Gate, from the field

scenes.name: Road down, following comets
scenes.what: Past the gate the road descends into the luminous city under comets; generations of faces line the way.
scenes.camera: drone or crane following POET down the processional road, tilt up to comet streaks
scenes.here: the processional road descending from the gate into the market

scenes.name: The city rises / here we are all one
scenes.what: Atlantis rises from the depths in golden light; diverse beings gather and look up together.
scenes.camera: extreme wide establishing as the city lifts, cut to POET in the gathering, faces lit from above
scenes.here: the round plaza

scenes.name: Jungle Interface and the heart-scan admission
scenes.what: Jungle merges into crystalline buildings over overgrown ruins; children and elders draw symbols in sand; a gate scans the POET's heart instead of a pass.
scenes.camera: handheld walk-through of vines on stone; insert of the heart-scan gate reading POET's chest
scenes.here: the hall of crystal trees

scenes.name: City Center: all safe
scenes.what: Back at the center, now fully alive; a ring of protective light encircles the community; unknown architecture glows.
scenes.camera: slow 360 orbit around POET in the plaza
scenes.here: the cathedral square, under the dish

scenes.name: Narrow streets by candlelight
scenes.what: POET walks stone alleys barely two people wide; candle flame blooms, shadows stretch, families gather behind lit windows, children's laughter, clouds set free.
scenes.camera: Steadicam behind POET down the alley (never a face-on EX; none present), candle close-ups, window POVs
scenes.here: the hidden stairwells, two people wide

scenes.name: Could stay forever, then wandering to the house
scenes.what: He sits a moment as Atlantis shines; voiceover ends ('welcoming me, & welcoming all'), he keeps wandering and arrives at a house where people are entering, and goes in.
scenes.camera: seated medium then wide; later documentary-style wandering (Mexico City footage) ending on a doorway with people filing in
scenes.here: the Container Rows to the House door

lines.text: The gates open with wings gifted from evolution, and made of marble stones
kissed by the hymns our creator composed with an orchestra of our ancestors wildest dreams to
welcome us. Poets who eased generations down yellow brick roads and plucked our souls out
of their secret places to follow comets to the capital city of our collective consciousness,
resurrecting Atlantis. Here we are all one. The pack we've made here with nature
abandon and hope for the best back on life. A relearned currency we reassess as a mission,
but here we are all safe. Here we are all one. The pack we've made here with nature
abandon and hope for the best back on life. A relearned currency we reassess as a mission,
but here we are all safe. An unfamiliar flickering candlelight illuminating smiles
at night where shadows cast from narrow streets beaming with love, and the joyful noises that
color rainbows, and give us infinite time to heal and set clouds free. I know my soul and
it could stay here forever, leaving behind crosshairs for continuums and strains for
serendipity. A city born in unison out of the purest of fictions welcoming me and welcoming all.

scenes.name: DJ drops in
scenes.what: Neon title over the booth; the DJ appears, spins, scratches; the fader slides and the crowd hushes waiting for the drop as the POET asks to be turned up.
scenes.camera: whip-pan to the booth, insert on the fader, wide of the hushed room
scenes.here: the House: the booth on the back wall

scenes.name: Eyes wide shut at the mic
scenes.what: POET at the bar, eyes closed, chin at the arch of the mic, opens his love story; strobe glints on his eyelids.
scenes.camera: tight profile close-up at the mic, slow push; reverse onto faces in the crowd
scenes.here: the bar, facing the floor

scenes.name: Ghosts in the speaker mesh
scenes.what: Transparent silhouettes drift through the speakers; vineyards and evergreen fields wilt in the projected light; treasures escape, stars on a marquee dim.
scenes.camera: macro on speaker mesh with superimposed silhouettes; cutaways to crowd watching
scenes.here: the speaker stacks

scenes.name: A thousand light years, into the red
scenes.what: He has walked across the greatest divide to be heard; on the second plea the VU meter slams into the red and the mic blooms.
scenes.camera: cut from galactic insert to VU meter close-up, then low angle on POET as the volume jumps
scenes.here: between bar and booth

scenes.name: Wedding bands and the boxed home
scenes.what: Rings orbit and drift apart; the shared home folds into a box; two moving vans split at a fork on one-way streets with arrowless signs and a blank billboard.
scenes.camera: projected inserts on the wall behind the POET; crowd silhouettes in the foreground
scenes.here: the projection wall: the container's steel side

scenes.name: Eleven years in daisy petals
scenes.what: Calendar pages spin off the turntable for eleven beats; petals fall on the vinyl; the DJ scratches 'love, love, not, not'; the mic is held out to empty space.
scenes.camera: overhead on the platter, petals under the needle; cut to the empty space beside POET
scenes.here: the platters

scenes.name: Rain, fog, dim lights, then chin high
scenes.what: The room picks its weather: storm waveform, fog across the floor lights, a dark cloud with a silver lining over the dancers. He turns to face delights and shadows, one night, tear and open mic at a time, chin now high, volume up.
scenes.camera: wide of the floor in haze with the cloud practical overhead; end on a low-angle close-up, POET's chin raised into the spotlight
scenes.here: the dance floor under the dark cloud

lines.text: DJ turn me up please. With eyes wide shut and my chin nested at the arc of the weight of these
spoken words, I have a story to tell. Of ghosts whispering unfolded delusions, birthed in purity
and dying and the veneers of sun-soaked evergreen fields are nourished. A love story of one by one
treasures escaping and devaluing themselves after defamed unsalted stars diminish their glares.
And I've walked a thousand light years across the greatest divide to be heard. So DJ please turn me
up. So I can speak of wedding bands diverging across abstract skies of wounded souls. Of a
shared home boxed in truck on separate one-way streets not built with u-turns or stop. Maybe
we shouldn't signs. A love story of years 11 years each plucked off as daisy pedals
we love we not. Of a future gone swiftly and a past left empty handed to pick a road of heavy rain
or a frontal fog or of dim night lights under a cloud with the silver lining. Of now turning
forth to face the lights and shadows one night at a time, one tear at a time. When called to a friend
at a time. One open mic at a time. Chin now nested high and volume turned up in a story to tell.

poems.title: Newly Single
poems.sound: Broken vinyl forms jagged heart on floor.

scenes.here: the subwoofer wall at the floor's edge

scenes.name: Mountains from the rooftop
scenes.what: The POET stares from the rooftop at unfamiliar yet relatable mountains in the distance, reaching toward something just beyond his fingertips.
scenes.camera: over-the-shoulder at the parapet, long lens compressing the ridgeline under a crescent moon
scenes.here: the parapet

lines.text: The soul has escaped my body for the moment and left him on the dance floor. He can now just be
flesh and bones, rejection and heartache hit differently when there are no feelings afloat.
I want my soul now to imagine my body pulsing and head throbbing from the music and empty on
a crowded floor of sweated perfumes and temptations. Let's watch strangers collide and spark electric
currents that gamut the mood, a good one. We want him to be the last one to leave, prolonging the
bitter refraction inside the walls of an escape that few pleasures offer us. Now let us put my
soul in the middle of an open field at the equator of a planet much larger than my own
and much hotter. Cool me down by pouring unfiltered water out of the ice bath salted from the closest
moons from angels of the newest religions and its joys capturing my body transiting in a flash of
strobe lights. Their gracious cursor blessed me, only infinity will tell. Now bring my soul back
to my body to lean back, breathe in the smoke that now fills the room and tell myself how good
it is to finally get acquainted with the night, staring into unfamiliar yet relatable mountains
in the distance and wandering eyes and wandering thoughts within reach.

poems.title: Yet Heard
poems.why: late night, moon up, wet pavement

scenes.name: The EX in the crowd
scenes.what: Leaving the club amid fawning crowds, the POET glimpses the EX from behind and reaches for him but cannot get through.
scenes.camera: handheld follow through the crowd; EX kept back-to-camera, soft focus, reaching hand in foreground
scenes.here: the sidewalk at the foot of the spire

scenes.name: Walking toward the moon
scenes.what: POET and EX walk down the Atlantis street together, talking, the moon at the end of the street; they 'grow old together' in feeling only (aging not literal).
scenes.camera: long tracking two-shot from behind (EX's face never shown), moon framed at the vanishing point; insert of both reflections in a puddle
scenes.here: the avenue toward the moon

scenes.name: Suitcases at the phone booth
scenes.what: EX and POET stand on the sidewalk near the phone booth with suitcases at their feet; the EX helps him pack to go.
scenes.camera: low shot at suitcase level, booth light spilling on the curb; EX present only as hands and back
scenes.here: the booth curb

scenes.name: The call to Mother
scenes.what: POET enters the booth and calls his MOTHER; they talk while watching the POET and EX break up on the sidewalk; cut to POET and MOTHER in her living room, the break-up still in the background. He hangs up and she disappears.
scenes.camera: through the booth glass with the break-up on the sidewalk behind; in the living room, a window frame holding the sidewalk scene (window inferred)
scenes.here: inside the booth (by phone: the mother's living room, the Overseer)

scenes.name: Father and son to the inner harbor
scenes.what: POET calls his FATHER, who appears from the yonders and watches the break-up; they walk paths east toward the sunrise and stroll the inner harbor, the break-up continuing in the background.
scenes.camera: wide walking shot along pier lights from behind, dawn ahead; break-up layered in the background plate
scenes.here: by phone: the Inner Harbour before dawn

scenes.name: The EX turns to haze
scenes.what: POET and EX are back on the sidewalk; the EX turns to haze and disappears, leaving the POET alone.
scenes.camera: locked-off wide two-shot; the EX dissolves out, hold on the POET alone at the curb
scenes.here: back at the booth curb

lines.text: Accepting you'll never say nor ever feel, my love was real.
What isn't mine I still cannot give.
I gather my things to go.
Before I go, we look at the moon the way we used to see it
and settle down the stillnessism.
We talk for years and travel through time
and it feels so good.
We grow old together.
I believe maybe we could have it all,
or swing in my humbled late nights and heartbreaks
and an end story unchanging.
You help me gather my things to go.
Before I go, I call on my mother.
In tears, speaking of an abyss, she's never known.
And we talk for years and we closet wounds
and we explain my way of birth then and even after prayer.
What isn't mine I still cannot give.
We grow old together with the moon looking at us
the way we used to be.
As my tears fall between the creases and faith,
dancing on my own, maternal ears in tune.
She watches us gather my things to go.
Before I go, I call on my father.
Summon his calming demeanor from the yonders
and we walk for years and travel east toward the sunrises
and retrace his footsteps now and then.
Guiding a settling down moon the way it used to leave
and my tears fall between the creases
and wave shadows of the inner harbor.
We stroll, father and son, hearted and shaken.
Someone borrowed and someone blew.
Yet broken, yet hurt.

poems.title: Magic Ride
poems.why: midnight through the last of the night to first light; tire spray on wet asphalt

scenes.name: The bike under the street lamp
scenes.what: The POET stands alone on the sidewalk and inspects a motorcycle parked beside him, idling under a street lamp, his face caught in the chrome mirror.
scenes.camera: wide of the empty sidewalk with the bike in lamplight, then a chrome-mirror insert
scenes.here: the same curb, the bike under the lamp

scenes.name: Mounting the machine
scenes.what: He rubs his aggressions into the steel, thumps the fender, swings a boot over the seat and laughs into the wind as he pulls away.
scenes.camera: tight inserts on gloved palms, fist on fender, boot swing; chrome panels reflecting the city
scenes.here: curbside

scenes.name: Loneliness through midnight intersections
scenes.what: He weaves through empty plazas, tunnels and midnight intersections with no one behind him; the real Mexico City motorcycle material covers this stretch.
scenes.camera: rear rig framing the empty pillion seat; goggles reflecting tunnel lights
scenes.here: empty plazas and the tunnels under the market

scenes.name: Swagger down the avenue
scenes.what: Riding through crowded streets with a swagger, one hand off the bars; eyes turn and heads twist as he passes.
scenes.camera: low-angle tracking on tire spray, whip-pans across crowd silhouettes, neon blur
scenes.here: the avenue under the LED canopy

scenes.name: Out of Atlantis as the moon settles
scenes.what: He rides out of Atlantis as the night turns and the sky lightens; the moon dips behind the skyline and a road sign points to a new dawn.
scenes.camera: wide from behind the rider leaving the city edge, skyline behind and dawn gradient ahead
scenes.here: the rail viaduct out of the city as the moon sets

scenes.name: Mountain road at first light
scenes.what: He rides through the mountains around Atlantis at first light, birdsong rising, leaning the bike into an impossible curve while a bystander's camera flashes.
scenes.camera: drone chase on mountain switchbacks, then a low side angle on the lean; snap-zoom bystander flash
scenes.here: the pass under the mountain, the rail beside the road

lines.text: I wasn't looking for a ride, but here you are, blissful and oddly sensitive,
withering a soul purveying both the dark and the light worlds I've known.
So I rub my aggressions into your steel coverings and hop on to amuse myself.
Loneliness is having everything with no one to tell,
being everywhere with no one to love and escape,
wide-eyed and stone but alive and well, wandering with no clear end.
I let the noise block the noise so the way I ride through the streets with the swag and eyes turn,
has twists, improve, yeah, the magic still exists.
All preparations to live and dream in darkness I no longer desire.
The moon settles and the tease of distant stars subsides
and I can see a morning ahead for me.
It looks like a morning I could believe in,
a morning where loss and life aren't so well, ripe with sunlight that's deceptively warm.
The tripping of birds, feeling of nests, spring out of the night that has covered me,
with my own curiosities for a chance at an end, where everything will be okay.
I want to live in this feeling forever, blissful and oddly innocent,
riding in a way you can't help but double-click,
improve, yeah, the magic still exists.

poems.title: New Day
poems.why: early morning just after dawn; mist on the distant sea

scenes.name: Arrival on the chilly shore
scenes.what: The motorcycle comes down out of the hills to the chapel shore; wide view of distant seas and the wooded hills behind.
scenes.camera: extreme wide from the water looking inland, bike small against the hills; slow push
scenes.here: the shore steps beneath the mountain

scenes.name: Remnants in the sunlight
scenes.what: Sun crosses the debris of the storm-wrecked chapel and the shattered tambourine from poem 3 (callback).
scenes.camera: low macro dolly across debris as light rakes across it; sun flare
scenes.here: the chapel's remnants in low sun

scenes.name: The temple builds itself
scenes.what: The POET starts to rebuild; the white futuristic temple rises in unison with his movements.
scenes.camera: locked-off time-lapse wide plus a tracking medium on the POET as walls assemble around him
scenes.here: the old footprint at the waterline

scenes.name: Choir chords in the new nave (inferred)
scenes.what: Inside the clean white hall the old choir stands and prayer lines return remade; sound calms him.
scenes.camera: symmetrical wide down the nave; sunbeam shafts; slow crane up
scenes.here: the new nave

scenes.name: Journal and the lonely mirror (inferred)
scenes.what: He opens a journal stored away and reads aloud; a mirror callback to the midnight solitude of earlier poems.
scenes.camera: close-up on pages and his profile; over-shoulder into a mirror
scenes.here: the mirror hall

scenes.name: Welcoming the new day
scenes.what: Doors open to full sun over the harbor; the finished temple stands bone-white and calm.
scenes.camera: reverse from inside the doors out to the sea, then wide exterior hero shot of the white temple
scenes.here: the threshold facing the harbour

lines.text: Even here is chilly in the morning.
River rafting fall covers the seas in the distance
and hugs the bases of tree-covered hills.
This world is at peace.
In silent resounds, choir chords calm the nerves of things I can't control
and offer them as keepsakes back to the higher powers.
Exhausted emotions carry forward a diminishing flame
to emit jazz tuned lyrics that heat and dry the morning dew.
All the remnants of the destruction revealed in the sunlight.
We can rebuild this temple.
It's a new day.
The catharsis evoked by loss in the painful crawl
along the cobblestone boulevards of broken dreams.
I can close a chapter and open a journal stored away
from moments of great clarity.
Words written from life's triumphs to offer a blueprint
of keeping faith alive and as majestic.
When words are read aloud and sung alone as gospels
to the lonely mirror's midnight hours,
the left tears drying with time that is common to past.
We can embrace a new day.
We can receive a new day.
We can welcome a new day.
Everything I've known and learned,
every circumference of life we're celebrating and believing
is here together in this sacred place,
reveling in the sunlight of a new beginning
with this world and a heart at peace.

poems.title: Reunion
poems.why: twilight and dusk, ending at a lit porch

scenes.name: Welcome home in the hall
scenes.what: Friends arrive under a welcome-home banner; laughter and hugs with no reason; the circle forms.
scenes.camera: wide master from the rafters, then handheld into the hugging circle
scenes.here: the hall under its rafters

scenes.name: Loud voices, overheard hearts
scenes.what: Voices peak; a chest-level glow pulses with every shout.
scenes.camera: tight chest-height mediums, shallow focus, fast cuts on laughter
scenes.here: the centre of the gathering

scenes.name: The empty rooms of the afterlife
scenes.what: The POET's mind drifts up into the rafters; a back room of empty chairs stands for the friends who are gone.
scenes.camera: tilt up into dim rafters; static wide of the dusty backroom
scenes.here: the rafters and a back room of empty chairs

scenes.name: Hourglasses and the group photo (archival reenactment)
scenes.what: Everyone freezes for a group photo, each holding an hourglass of burning sand; old photos reenacted, maps of shared routes.
scenes.camera: locked frontal group tableau matched to the archival photo; macro on falling grains
scenes.here: the hall's front, posed like the photographs

scenes.name: Trees at the forest edge
scenes.what: Outside, friends touch tree trunks under picnic lights; breath mingles in cool dusk; memories project onto fog.
scenes.camera: low angle up into the canopy; slow lateral track along the trunks
scenes.here: the grounds where the hill's woods begin

scenes.name: Brotherhood chain
scenes.what: Wrists interlock, heads lean together; one ear pressed to the next brother's chest.
scenes.camera: profile tracking shot down the listening chain; extreme close-up of an ear on a chest
scenes.here: the sandy path to the shore

scenes.name: Football in the meadow, then home
scenes.what: A football spirals across a sunset meadow; polaroids scatter; the group walks up as a porch light switches on.
scenes.camera: wide golden-hour meadow with the ball arcing through frame; closing shot from behind the group toward a lit porch
scenes.here: the meadow, ending at a porch

lines.text: Decades later, there was less time for words and more space for laughter, hugs with no reason,
loud voices so our hearts can be overheard. My mind drifts into the darkness of our afterlives,
and those rooms are empty. We are all here, each holding our glasses of burning sands
and known journeys, and grateful to every living tree in the forest for the shared years
and the shared memories. This is brotherhood. Smiles with no reason,
narrow differences so our hearts can be overheard. Decades later, we can place our ears upon the next
brother's soul and follow paths of hilltops and canyons, of blinding lights and infinite nights,
all too familiar and create the type of space for laughter
and football and recollections that bring us home every time.

poems.title: How to Win My Heart
poems.why: daytime; haze gathering over the harbor at the end

scenes.name: Walk from the temple around the harbor
scenes.what: The POET wanders alone from the new temple along the harbor to the cafe.
scenes.camera: long lens lateral track along the promenade, water and boats between camera and POET
scenes.here: the promenade from the temple round the harbour

scenes.name: The corner cafe table
scenes.what: He sits at a corner table and observes couples at other tables, wanting to be noticed.
scenes.camera: static medium on the POET at the corner table, couples soft in the foreground; eyeline cuts to the tables
scenes.here: the pier café's corner table

scenes.name: Distances, younger selves, praying elders
scenes.what: Cutaways: silhouettes on opposite shores, ghost children behind glass, an old couple praying together at church.
scenes.camera: reflections in the cafe window double his face with the ghost children; quiet wide in a church pew for the elders
scenes.here: the café glass; a harbour church

scenes.name: Victory-less seasons (inner montage)
scenes.what: From his seat: a lone traveler, burning diary, love letters blown away, dusty trophy cases, flowers frozen in ice.
scenes.camera: push in on his still face, then match-cuts into the montage
scenes.here: the table (mental space)

scenes.name: Harvesting the poppies
scenes.what: Fields of scarlet poppies and purple blossoms are harvested and become the POET's power.
scenes.camera: aerial over flower fields; light flowing into his chest in a close-up
scenes.here: the Night Garden Field by day, harvested

scenes.name: From a distant window
scenes.what: Still at the cafe watching couples; hope that someone will notice him and meet his eyes.
scenes.camera: through-the-glass shot from outside the cafe; rack focus from reflection to his eyes; iris close-up
scenes.here: the café window from the harbour

scenes.name: Stands and walks the harbor
scenes.what: He leaves the cafe and walks around the harbor as haze starts to gather on the water.
scenes.camera: follow from behind along the waterline; widen as haze rises off the water
scenes.here: the harbour edge and piers, the haze rising

lines.text: I want you to notice me in a corner cafe
at the Harbor of the Heavens, wandering in thought,
discovering water on Jupiter's moons,
healing the sick with silent prayers
and molding a better world to return to
with every pulsing beat after walking alone.
I want you to really notice me
with the distances we couldn't avoid
and our younger selves watching and dreaming,
while our elders clutch their pearls,
hold their faith and breath closely,
freeing their worries peacefully.
I've journeyed beyond any place you can conceivably be.
So I thought, life has burned all of my love stories.
All ends led to losses,
victory-less seasons for a man that wanted just one win.
I could celebrate forever.
Ice has frozen in thought,
friendships in death and departure.
I've learned to love myself more,
manage loss and harvest a wizardry more brilliant
than the scarlet poppies and purple blossoms
at time and tears have just claimed.
Yet from a distant window, beautiful and calm,
hope tells me you'll see me.
And if you notice me and capture my eyes
as you refocus yours,
stepping back and letting them say hello,
all the fatigue of wandering alone in thought,
in windless seasons and scarlet poppies
won't prevent me from sharing a smile
worth the promise of my heart.

poems.title: Hot Minute
poems.why: timeless; the party reads as night

scenes.name: Taken by the haze
scenes.what: Haze rises from the ground and covers him; he is reluctant at first, then gives in.
scenes.camera: slow tilt up the body as haze climbs; hand gripping a frame edge in close-up
scenes.here: the harbour edge, then the end of the catwalk

scenes.name: Floating in the black
scenes.what: He floats alone in black, as after the poem 1 fall.
scenes.camera: static frame with the POET slowly rotating in black; frame cracks on 'terminated'
scenes.here: the centre of the void

scenes.name: Cross-cut: highs and lows of life
scenes.what: The film cuts back and forth between the floating POET and B-roll human scenes; the machines are unplugged.
scenes.camera: hard cuts on the beat between void and documentary B-roll
scenes.here: void and B-roll

scenes.name: Battle scars and graytones
scenes.what: Still floating; light traces his scars; gray brushed into his sight after defeats.
scenes.camera: macro along skin and scars; desaturating grade
scenes.here: void

scenes.name: The vintage door appears
scenes.what: Still floating in all black, an old vintage door materializes.
scenes.camera: wide of the lone door in black, POET entering frame from behind
scenes.here: before the door

scenes.name: The dance at the vintage party
scenes.what: He enters the old-time vintage party; guests move in romantic slow motion; a dance.
scenes.camera: Steadicam following through the slow-motion crowd from behind; overhead on two dancers under one spotlight
scenes.here: the ballroom beyond the door

scenes.name: Disappears into the crowd; door closes
scenes.what: He disappears into the crowd from the back; the door closes on the viewer. END.
scenes.camera: hold on the back of the crowd as he vanishes; reverse from the void as the door swings shut to black
scenes.here: the doorway, from outside

lines.text: Don't make me leave and go where promises, hearts,
spectrums of light-filled constellations are broken.
I escaped here for a reason,
believing this would give me a sharpened key of answers
in a more grounded bravado
for my life of conquests and queries.
The way you see things felt safe and timeless.
Whatever has terminated this moment, damn you,
but let it feel love and lost as we must endure,
absent artificial escapes and machine learning strengths
for my highs and lows as resource materials.
Well, I can't leave behind the impulse
that comes from battle scars
and can't leave behind the wisdom that brushes gray tones
into our melanin after disappointments and defeats.
I trust that you'll be fine.
I escaped here for a reason.
Our dance together is a victory to entwine muses,
immersed in twisted dons for a hot minute,
and a genesis of a New Testament as it ends.
